articles.headline: The Utah Royals stun the San Diego Wave 1-0 in the NWSL quarterfinals
keyFacts: The seventh-seeded Utah Royals defeated the second-seeded San Diego Wave 1-0 in the National Women’s Soccer League quarterfinals Friday night.
Forward Kiana Palacios scored the game’s only goal in the 30th minute following a cross from Cloé Lacasse.
The Utah Royals will advance to the semifinals to play either the Washington Spirit or the Portland Thorns.
body: SAN DIEGO (AP) — The seventh-seeded Utah Royals earned their first ever playoff win by upsetting the No. 2 seeded San Diego Wave 1-0 in the quarterfinals of the National Women’s Soccer League playoffs Friday night.

Forward Cloé Lacasse delivered a pinpoint low-driven cross to Kiana Palacios, who took a touch and fired it home for the game’s lone goal in he 30th minute. It was the first time the visitors have led the Wave during the 2026 season in all competitions.
Goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn made four saves for her sixth clean sheet.
“Unbelievable, it’s just everything you could hope for,” McGlynn said. “I’m like in shock, no words can describe this feeling.”

The Royals snapped a four-match winless streak and will now head on the road to take on either the third-seeded Washington Spirit or the sixth-seeded Portland Thorns in the semifinals. The Spirit host the Thorns on Sunday in their quarterfinal.

Both teams were missing key players as San Diego midfielder Kimmi Ascanio was unavailable due to a thigh injury and Utah midfielder Mina Tanaka, who was initially listed as questionable with a hamstring injury, was ruled out for the match.
The home side were held scoreless despite having the advantage in possession (62%-38%), shots (16-8), and shots on target (5-2).
The Wave came into the match on a seven-match unbeaten streak, but have now dropped their fourth consecutive playoff match.

articles.headline: Valparaiso stuns Purdue: Buzzer-beating 3-pointer in 2OT sends Boilermakers to first 0-2 start since 1976
keyFacts: Valparaiso defeated Purdue 83-80 in double overtime on Friday night after guard Justus McNair hit a buzzer-beating 3-pointer.
The loss dropped 19.5-point favorites Purdue to an 0-2 start for the first time since the 1976-77 season.
The defeat snapped Purdue's 23-game home winning streak in November and was their first home loss to a Missouri Valley Conference opponent since 1978.
body: Another major upset in college basketball headlined on Friday night in West Lafayette, Indiana, when Valparaiso handed Purdue a stunning 83-80 loss in double overtime. With the game tied at 80 in the final seconds, Valpo guard Justus McNair knocked down a corner 3-pointer as time expired to hand Purdue its second loss of the season.
Valpo sent the game to double overtime after Rakim Chaney knocked down a 3-pointer at the buzzer to tie the game at 70. The Boilermakers led by as many as 15 points in the first half.

The Boilermakers were 19.5-point favorites against Valparaiso and are now 0-2 for the first time since the 1976-77 season. Purdue is the latest high-major team to suffer a stunning loss during the opening week of the season. On opening night, Oklahoma lost to East Texas A&M as a 28.5-point favorite.

Purdue was riding a 23-game home winning streak during November. The loss to Valpo marked the first loss against a Missouri Valley Conference opponent at Mackey Arena since 1978, when Purdue lost to a Larry Bird-led Indiana State team.

The Boilermakers are in the midst of a major transition after Braden Smith, Trey Kaufman-Renn and Fletcher Loyer departed the program. That trio was among the most experienced in the sport and helped Purdue reach the Elite Eight in their final season together. Kaufman-Renn, of course, is playing his sixth season of college basketball with Kansas after being granted a motion for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA.

articles.headline: State Dept. offers $20 million reward for information about Iran’s nuke program
keyFacts: The Trump administration is offering up to $20 million through the State Department for information about Iran's nuclear program.
The US government is seeking details on Iranian nuclear scientists, technologies, and associated organizations via secure messaging apps and offers possible relocation as an incentive.
US officials stated that Qatari officials are mediating fresh discussions with Tehran about its nuclear program following recent airstrikes.
body: The Trump administration is offering the public up to $20 million in exchange for information about Iran’s nuclear program.
The bounty is being offered through the State Department’s Rewards for Justice Program.

Specifically, the US is seeking information about Iranian “nuclear scientists and staff,” “nuclear program-related technologies and capabilities” and “associated organizations and personnel,” according to the announcement, which was posted on X.
“If you have information on Iran’s nuclear program, assets, or associated individuals, send it to us,” Rewards for Justice asked the public.
People wishing to provide the US government with intel can send information via an encrypted Tor browser tip line or use the secure Signal or Telegram messaging apps.
In an apparent effort to get Iranians to share their insights, Rewards for Justice is also offering “possible relocation” as another incentive for information.
The bounty page notes that the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) reported in 2025 that Iran was enriching uranium to 60% purity, which is close to the level necessary for a nuclear weapon.

“The regime’s lack of compliance with the IAEA on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges,” Rewards for Justice said.
US Central Command, the military group tasked with carrying out the Iran war, shared the bounty on its social media platforms as well.

The Trump administration previously used Rewards for Justice in March to offer $10 million for information about 10 key leaders of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, which the US government labels a terrorist group.
“I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I’ll have to. You’ll know soon enough,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office Thursday.
A US official told The Post that Qatari officials have been mediating fresh discussions with Tehran about its nuclear program.
At least three meetings on “concrete proposals” have occurred in the past week, The New York Times first reported, with summits in Tehran and Doha.
Trump has repeatedly said Iran was close to developing a nuclear weapon, which he believes the regime would’ve used to target countries in the Middle East, including Israel.
The president maintains the 8-month-long war has been a success because Iran’s navy, missile and drone facilities, and nuclear sites have been devastated by US airstrikes.

articles.headline: President Herzog faces key choice as Israel struggles to form government
keyFacts: Israeli President Isaac Herzog must decide who gets the first attempt at forming a government, after an inconclusive election left both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival, former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, short of a parliamentary majority.
Herzog has said he will task a candidate with forming a government on Sunday.

Eisenkot has received the endorsement of a majority of lawmakers – but only thanks to parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats in October’s election, but whom Eisenkot has ruled out bringing into government.
body: Israeli President Isaac Herzog must decide who gets the first attempt at forming a government, after an inconclusive election left both Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival, former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, short of a parliamentary majority.

Herzog has said he will task a candidate with forming a government on Sunday. Eisenkot has received the endorsement of a majority of lawmakers – but only thanks to parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel, which won a record 19 seats in October’s election, but whom Eisenkot has ruled out bringing into government.
Here is what we know:
Who is Herzog likely to ask to form a government?
During consultations between party heads and Herzog, which ended on Thursday, 67 out of 120 Knesset members endorsed Eisenkot, while only 46 endorsed Netanyahu.

Netanyahu’s endorsements fell seven short of his bloc’s 53 seats after United Torah Judaism, one of his longtime allies, withheld endorsements over his coalition’s failure to exempt ultra-Orthodox Israelis from military service.

Herzog has not publicly committed to either side, saying that while the numbers may look clear, “mutual vetoes between the blocs and within the blocs themselves” made it hard to tell who could build a coalition.
Prior to the October 27 elections, reports emerged that the president wanted to push for a national unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot’s rival parties to avoid another election.
How difficult will it be to form a government?

No bloc has secured the 61 seats needed to form a majority government. Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious alliance has 53, four Jewish-led parties backing Eisenkot hold 48, and the Arab-led parties hold 19.

Eisenkot has ruled out forming a government with the Arab-led parties, which would give him a 67-seat bloc. Winning over the two ultra-Orthodox parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas, would give him exactly 61 seats.
United Torah Judaism has signalled that its support was available for the right price, but Shas endorsed Netanyahu on Wednesday.

Netanyahu, meanwhile, would need to lure an opposition party to his side. A unity government with the two men rotating as prime minister – and excluding Arab-led parties from government – is another option, but many Netanyahu rivals have ruled out serving under him.
Will Arab-led parties be part of the next government?
So far, it seems unlikely that they will.
The Arab-led parties are the Joint List, an alliance of three parties, and the United Arab List (Ra’am). They hold 11 and eight seats, respectively.
Ra’am says it is willing to join an Eisenkot-led government, while the Joint List has ruled out joining but offered to help put him in office from the outside.

Both endorsed Eisenkot during consultations with President Herzog, but he has refused to bring either into government unless they meet certain conditions, including recognising Hamas as a “terrorist organisation”.

Ra’am leader Mansour Abbas, whose party joined an anti-Netanyahu coalition in 2021 and became the first party representing Palestinians to enter government in Israel, has expressed support for disarming Hamas, but declined to label it as a “terror” group.
However, Israeli law allows Eisenkot to become prime minister with fewer than 61 seats if his proposed government wins a parliamentary confidence vote – which the two could help him secure.
Eisenkot could form a minority government in the meantime and later secure a majority by luring the two ultra-Orthodox parties by making concessions on the conscription issue.

In positions that many observers see as highlighting the second-class nature of Palestinian citizens in Israel, some of Eisenkot’s allies have opposed any reliance on Palestinian lawmakers, while Netanyahu’s Likud has threatened that cooperating with the Arab-led parties would be “dangerous to Israel”.
Senior Joint List member Ahmad Tibi told The Associated Press that rejecting a partnership would prove Israel is “an ethnocracy, not an absolute democracy for all citizens”.
What do Palestinian-led parties want from the next government?
First, an end to Netanyahu’s rule.
The Joint List said its unanimous backing for Eisenkot answered a “public demand” to stop Netanyahu and his government returning to power.

By widening Eisenkot’s lead, it said, it hoped to narrow the path to a unity government that keeps Netanyahu in office. Its support, it added, did not mean dropping its reservations about an opposition that had not shown readiness to confront Netanyahu’s approach or incitement against Palestinian citizens of Israel.

In return for outside support, Arab-led parties are seeking guarantees for Palestinian citizens, including an end to house demolitions and incitement, action against crime, and a political horizon for Palestinians.

Tibi told The AP he had no illusions that this would end Israel’s wars or bring a Palestinian state, but said a “repair government” would improve Palestinian citizens’ lives, including, potentially, by tackling violent crime in their communities.
Ra’am leader Abbas has also said ending the government of Netanyahu, and far-right figures such as Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, is a priority.
What happens if no government can be formed?
The nominee chosen by Herzog will have 28 days to form a coalition, extendable by 14 more. If they fail, another nominee will be chosen and granted 28 days.
If the second nominee fails, a parliament majority can back a third candidate, and be granted a final 14 days.
If once again no government is formed, the Knesset will be dissolved and an entirely new election called within 90 days. This would mean Netanyahu staying on as caretaker prime minister.

Nehru Jamhour, an analyst of Israeli affairs, told Al Jazeera that this drawn-out impasse was the likeliest outcome, and Netanyahu’s preferred one. He said that Netanyahu was hoping that a repeat election could weaken his rivals and depress turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel.

articles.headline: DeSantis blasts Washington Post over report he's preparing 2028 presidential bid
keyFacts: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis denied a Washington Post report claiming he is preparing a 2028 presidential campaign.
The Post reported that DeSantis contacted political consultants and sent a fundraising text, citing anonymous sources briefed on his plans.
DeSantis called the report fabricated on social media and stated he has not reached out to anyone about running.
body: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis fired back Friday at a report that he is preparing another White House bid in 2028, accusing The Washington Post of fabricating claims that he has started reaching out to political consultants about a potential campaign.
"The Washington Post is fabricating this out of whole cloth," DeSantis wrote on X. "I have not reached out to anybody about running for anything."
"Just another pathetic attempt to garner clicks. Using anonymous sources of course!" he added.
The Post reported Friday, citing three people briefed on his plans, that DeSantis was preparing to seek the Republican presidential nomination in 2028.
VANCE, CRUZ AND DESANTIS DIAGNOSE GOP'S MIDTERM DISASTER AS BATTLE OVER PARTY'S FUTURE BEGINS

The newspaper reported that DeSantis, who unsuccessfully ran for president in 2024 and is term-limited after 2026, had already reached out to at least one national political consultant about working on a prospective campaign.
A federal super PAC tied to DeSantis also sent out a fundraising text earlier this week, The Post reported.
DeSantis continued pushing back against the report in exchanges with social media users.
When one user expressed hope that The Post's reporting was accurate, the governor replied that he was "sorry to disappoint."
DeSantis also responded to another user who suggested political consultants may have been using his name to attract attention.
"Probably the case. But maybe just made up by WaPo," he wrote.
FIRST MUSLIM SENATOR, FIRST BLACK FEMALE GOVERNOR: 2026 MIDTERM ELECTION RESULTS MAKE HISTORY

Speculation surrounding DeSantis' political future comes just days after Republicans suffered sweeping defeats in the midterm elections , losing control of both chambers of Congress and several traditionally Republican strongholds.
The Sunshine State, however, remained a bright spot for the GOP, with Republican Byron Donalds winning the governor's race.

"This is close to an extinction-level event for Republicans," DeSantis said Wednesday, warning that among the nation's 10 most populous states, Florida would be the only one with Republican control of its government.
DESANTIS CALLS GOP MIDTERM LOSSES 'EXTINCTION-LEVEL EVENT' — AND EXPLAINS WHY FLORIDA SURVIVED
DeSantis previously sought the 2024 Republican presidential nomination but suspended his campaign in January 2024 after the Iowa caucuses and endorsed Donald Trump.
The governor, who will leave office in January, has previously left open the possibility of another presidential campaign .
Fox News Digital has reached out to DeSantis' office and The Washington Post for comment.
Fox News Digital's Charles Creitz contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Sequoia shutting down its Scouts program marks the end of an era
keyFacts: Venture capital firm Sequoia announced it is shutting down its pioneering scout program as part of a broad overhaul.
Observers note the decision reflects a changing venture investing landscape where the traditional scout model has reached its limits.
Industry experts expect scout programs to be revamped rather than disappear entirely as firms shift toward more focused strategies.
body: Sequoia this week announced a broad overhaul in a memo posted to X, a move that includes closing its London office and shutting down its scout program. Observers warn that it would be a mistake to read too much into the London closure, since the British capital has a thriving AI scene. On the other hand, the decision to end scouts says more about where venture investing is headed.

That’s partly because 17 years ago, Sequoia pioneered the scouts model, in which select founders and operators write checks on the firm’s behalf. Amid increased competition for deal flow, many VC firms followed suit. But a consensus now seems to be emerging that the model has reached its limits in its current form.

Not everyone was sold on the model in the first place. “They pioneered the scout program but [to be honest] it never made sense to me!” VC Sheel Mohnot wrote on X this week. “The scouts themselves don’t really care that much about the investments, you can still miss (like they did with Uber), not sure what it gets you. I suspect other firms will shutter theirs too.” he added.

To be clear, Sequoia didn’t make a case against scouts in the memo. Instead, it framed its decision as part of a broader need for more focus. But its goal of “putting more energy behind fewer people and things” is likely to resonate with others who’ve questioned the ‘spray and pray’ approach to scouting.

Rival firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), for instance, rolled out a global scout network aimed at spotting opportunities in the U.S. and also in smaller European hubs. But a16z partner Gabriel Vasquez told TechCrunch earlier this year that the firm had revamped its program to double down “on the best people.”

Under this new approach, Vasquez explained, scouts get more resources but are also expected to be more active, such as by co-hosting dinners with the firm. “They get more budget, but we have reduced the number,” he said.

This also seems to indicate that it is VC firms that have been driving an overhaul of the model. For founders, being a scout is attractive: it brings them closer to firms they may want checks from someday, or even a partner role with, and being seen as someone who can write a check can raise their standing among other founders.

Some scouts will undoubtedly mourn the end of Sequoia’s program. Among them is Station F boss Roxanne Varza, who wrote on LinkedIn that she was “sad” to hear that the program was getting cut off, and “hope[d] that other funds [w]on’t follow suit.”

Varza, a former Sequoia scout from 2020 to 2025, told TechCrunch that she had no information beyond what has been shared publicly, but observed that becoming a scout had often been a stepping stone for aspiring investment managers.

“I cannot name all of the incredible scouts that have gone on to join or build funds, but there are quite a few. And the scout programs may have helped them get there — allowed them to build an investment track record, allowed them to build relationships with various funds directly, and more,” she wrote to TechCrunch.

According to Varza, the program’s impact went beyond the individual level, instead helping the entire ecosystem become more mature. “I believe they have helped to foster the investment culture and early-stage investment landscape that we now see in Europe, for example,” Varza said.

While others may agree with Varza about the role these programs have played, they may still have run their course for two reasons. First, seasoned operators may get more financial upside as angels. When it’s their own money, they get to keep the returns, too. Second, leading VC firms are now big and well-known enough that the best founders tend to come to them, so they worry less about missing deals, except at the very earliest stages or in niches and geographies where they have less reach.

Still, the pull of those early and niche deals is why scouts programs are much more likely to get revamped than to disappear entirely. “While Sequoia may be cutting the program, venture partner-style deals are likely to continue,” said Varza in her email to TechCrunch. “Scouts was just a way to scale the format. I don’t imagine Sequoia would end all forms of venture partners, but they are full of surprises.”

articles.headline: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director says King Art considered adding other factions to the game like Death Guard, but decided on Adeptus Mechanicus because 'lore-wise' it's the most 'interesting in terms of gameplay'
keyFacts: King Art considered adding factions like Death Guard to Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 before selecting the Adeptus Mechanicus, creative director Jan Theysen said.
Theysen said the Adeptus Mechanicus was chosen because it is the most important lore faction missing from past games and offers unique gameplay compared to other armies.
The game is scheduled for release on December 3 and will feature four separate faction campaigns.
body: - Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director Jan Theysen says King Art considered adding other playable factions besides Adeptus Mechanicus
- Theysen says the team played around with the idea of adding Death Guard, but it was too similar to other factions
- He says Adeptus Mechanicus is "lore-wise" the "most important faction that never was part of a Dawn of War"

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4 creative director Jan Theysen has revealed that King Art considered adding other playable factions that didn't make the cut, but felt Adeptus Mechanicus was the best fit for the fourth option.

Dawn of War 4 will feature four separate faction campaigns for the Space Marines, Orks, Necrons, and Adeptus Mechanicus, which the creative confirmed was "the first thing we decided" because Dawn of War, and Warhammer in general, "is fundamentally about the factions" and "how weird and crazy and cool they are."

But why Adeptus Mechanicus, a faction that has never been playable before? According to Theysen, who discussed the upcoming game at length in an interview with TechRadar Gaming, the studio wanted to do "a modern version, if you like" of the first Dawn of War game and knew Orks should be included since they "are just very Dawn of War," along with the character Gorgutz.

Then it wanted Necrons to be playable as well, because the team thought it would be "interesting because they were kind of promised for Dawn of War 3 and never came." He added, "We felt like it's a nice gesture to eventually bring them in."
After adding the Space Marines as the third playable faction, one spot remained, but before choosing Adeptus Mechanicus, aka AdMech, it considered other factions first.

"We said, okay, is there anything that never was part of a Dawn of War game officially that we could bring to the game and introduce for everybody, and there are a handful of factions, but not that many," Theysen said. "We looked into Death Guard or even Leagues of Votann. But in the end AdMech is by far the like biggest and, lore-wise, most important faction that never was part of a Dawn of War."

Theysen called AdMech the most "interesting in terms of gameplay" and "how we thought the faction should feel" compared to a faction like Death Guard, which is "a relatively slow army," and it already had Necrons and Space Marines that are "very tanky."

articles.headline: US asks China to uphold Busan trade deal commitments
keyFacts: US officials urged China to immediately fulfill its commitments under the 2025 trade agreement, including rare earth minerals and agricultural purchases.
Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng expressed serious concern over recent US trade restrictions during a videoconference with US officials.
Both nations agreed to continue cooperation and manage differences, with leaders expected to meet at the upcoming APEC forum.
body: Top officials of United States President Donald Trump's administration have called on China to "fully and immediately" implement its commitments under a 2025 trade agreement between the two nations, including on rare earth and other critical minerals.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on Friday held a videoconference with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng on the trade and economic relationship between Washington and Beijing, a statement from Greer's office said.

Greer "emphasized the critical importance of China taking concrete actions to fully implement its past commitments, particularly as they relate to agricultural purchases, rare earths, and other critical minerals.” it added.
The US-China trade agreement

The US officials were referring to an accord reached between the world's two largest economies in 2025 in a meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in South Korea's Busan, on the sidelines of an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
The deal had been reached during a period that saw the two countries exchange tariff escalations prompted by Trump's wider tariffs policy, which particularly targeted China, among other countries.
The accord capped US tariffs on Chinese goods — enforced during Trump's second stint as president — at about 20%.
China agreed to buy 25 million metric tons of US soybeans for the next three years.
Beijing also said it would keep China's rare earth exports flowing, suspending new export curbs.
The minerals are critical for the technological industry, and the Trump administration has in the past complained that Beijing was not meeting its commitments regarding supply.

"The Trump Administration will continue pursuing policies that benefit American workers, farmers, and businesses and strengthen our economic and national security,” Bessent wrote on X after the high-level call.
China raises concern over US trade restrictions

He, who is Beijing's lead negotiator on trade ties with the US, during Friday's interaction expressed "serious concern" over recent US trade restrictions targeting his country, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.
The report did not elaborate which measure the vice premier was referring to.
But both parties agreed to "continuously strengthen cooperation”and "properly manage differences" to promote a "stable" US-China trade relationship, Xinhua said.
The Busan trade deal at first covered only one year, but the US and China extended their trade pact until January 10 next year, as Trump hosted Xi at the White House in September.
The two leaders are expected to meet again at the upcoming APEC forum in Shenzhen, China, slated from November 18 to 19.

Meanwhile, in a separate development, China has confirmed for the first time that it is discussing a historic trilateral summit of Xi, Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the APEC gathering.

China "is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state,” Mao Ning, a spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry, said at a media briefing in Beijing this week.

articles.headline: House GOP Oversight chairman says ‘there’s a lot of questions about Hegseth’
keyFacts: House Oversight Chairman James Comer declined to back Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, stating there are many questions about him.
The House will vote next week on impeachment articles against Hegseth filed by Representative Thomas Massie following Republican election losses.
President Donald Trump stated on 60 Minutes that he maintains full confidence in Hegseth despite the growing scrutiny.
body: House Oversight Chairman James Comer (R-KY) declined to back Secretary of War Pete Hegseth as an impeachment vote against the secretary looms, saying there are “a lot of questions” about him.

The House must vote next week on impeachment articles filed by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) prior to the midterm elections. Frustrations over high prices due to the prolonged war in Iran led to staggering Republican losses in Tuesday’s elections, putting increased attention on Hegseth and his role in the conflict.
Comer, a staunch Trump ally, sidestepped on whether he would like to see a new war secretary when asked during an appearance on NewsNation.
“Well, that’s going to be a decision that President Trump’s going to have to make,” said Comer.

“But I can tell you with a high level of confidence that … there’s a lot of questions about Hegseth. We have no idea what the strategy is moving forward in Iran. No one’s happy about Iran, and I think the Republican voters are more upset about what’s going on in Iran than the Democrat voters,” Comer added.

Comer’s thinly veiled criticism comes as he positions himself for a potential run for Kentucky governor, where he is likely the odds-on favorite. Anger over the war in Iran and its effect on gas prices triggered unexpected results in Kentucky and other heavily agricultural areas on Tuesday, including a stunning loss in a Kentucky congressional district Trump carried by roughly 15 points in 2024.

Despite renewed scrutiny of Hegseth following the Democratic sweep in the elections, in his first post-midterm interview, Trump told 60 Minutes that he had full confidence in Hegseth, waving off speculation that he could be on the chopping block.

articles.headline: The 8 Best Castlevania Games Of All Time, Ranked
keyFacts: Polygon published a ranked list of the eight best Castlevania video games of all time.
The list includes classic 8-bit and 16-bit titles, modern releases, and historical context for each game.
Castlevania: Symphony of the Night was ranked as the top game in the franchise.
body: Castlevania is one of the most beloved franchises in video game history, despite a period of 13 years when we didn’t see a new installment until the launch of Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse earlier this year.

Over the years, the games have provided a variety of experiences, mixed with rich lore built on the vampire myth. With so many games available to choose from, it can be difficult to know where to begin if you haven’t touched the series in a while. Accordingly, here is our ranked list of the 8 best Castlevania games. It should make an excellent starting point.
8 Super Castlevania 4
Released: Oct. 31, 1991

When Castlevania came to the Super Nintendo, it needed to impress players who were still deciding whether they wanted to spend money on a new generation of Nintendo hardware. Fortunately for everyone involved, the team at Konami was up to the task. Super Castlevania 4 features beautiful environments, as well as a hero who can now whip in eight directions, even while jumping. It’s also possible to grapple to distant points, or to wield the whip as a shield. Early use of Mode 7 rotation provided some visual showpieces to go along with parallax depth that brought static environments to life. The adventure starts outside the castle, allowing Simon to explore its harsh exterior before venturing inside for a final showdown with the lord of the manor. If you’re looking for a starting point, you could do much worse, and it’s conveniently available as part of the Castlevania Anniversary Collection on Switch, PlayStation 4, PC, and Xbox One.
7 Castlevania: Bloodlines
Released: Mar. 17, 1994

The Super Nintendo wasn’t the only hardware to feature a high-quality Castlevania game during the 16-bit era. Castlevania: Bloodlines took a unique approach, introducing a hero who strikes with a spear. He can use it to access alternate routes that the other character (who fights with a more traditional whip) cannot. The pacing was fast and furious, in keeping with many Genesis games of that time. The setting was also more modern than the other classic titles, taking place during the first World War. Stages are inspired by locations around the globe, including a visit to the Leaning Tower of Pisa, among other attractions. Throw in some stunning visual tricks that made full use of the Genesis hardware, along with a beautiful score from composer Michiru Yamane (who would go on to compose for Symphony of the Night) and you have a truly special entry in the franchise.
6 Castlevania Chronicles
Released: July 23, 1993

Originally developed for the Sharp X68000 and released on that hardware as Akumajo Dracula, Castlevania Chronicles was one of the final Castlevania games built in the classical style. It actually is a remake of 1986’s first entry in the series. 1993’s version offered greatly improved visuals and sound, while providing generally fair but challenging gameplay that is some of the most difficult the series ever offered. Some new twists maintain the element of surprise, even as players retread familiar ground, but there’s no better way to experience the original adventure, as its developers intended. When I checked earlier this year, the digital version of the prettied up PlayStation port was still available to purchase through the PlayStation Store on a PlayStation 3 console, if you add the funds to your wallet on newer hardware. Or you can hunt down a physical copy of that port, which should play just fine on your PlayStation 3.
5 Castlevania: Rondo of Blood
Released: Oct. 29, 1993

If more people had easily been able to play the game as its developers intended, Castlevania: Rondo of Blood might be remembered today as the premier Castlevania experience. Sadly, the game remained exclusive to the PC Engine CD hardware for a long time. It didn’t head to North America and Europe until it arrived on PSP as part of 2007’s Castlevania: The Dracula X Chronicles collection, and as a Virtual Console selection in 2010, almost a decade and a half after its initial release. The closest we got in the meantime was Dracula X on the Super Nintendo. That title was a mostly unsuccessful attempt to compress Rondo of Blood’s essence to fit on a cartridge — and to reach hardware that hadn’t bombed outside of Japan. The same plot and characters returned, as did many enemy sprites. Both games began in a town on fire. However, the branching stages were absent, replaced by abbreviated challenges that players found frustrating. Some characters from the original version weren’t even playable, and the sound quality suffered immensely. Rondo of Blood is an important game in Castlevania’s timeline, and concludes with the events that serve as a prologue to Symphony of the Night. If you haven’t yet done so, you should play through it soon.
4 Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow
Released: May 6, 2003

Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow followed one year after Harmony of Dissonance, which in some respects was the more spectacular of the pair. But despite its inferior visuals, Aria of Sorrow offered the richer experience on a mechanical level. Players control Soma Cruz, who blacks out during the first solar eclipse of the century and awakens in Dracula’s castle. There, he finds he can absorb the essence of the monsters he vanquishes, a useful way to gain the strength he’ll need to reach Dracula’s throne room and rescue his classmate. The adventure is surprisingly complex, given the tiny hardware that houses it, and still a lot of fun to play. You can most easily experience it and other games of that era as part of Castlevania Advance Collection on Switch, PlayStation 4, PC, and Xbox One.
3 Castlevania 3: Dracula’s Curse
Released: Dec. 22, 1989

The 8-bit era established Castlevania as a force to be reckoned with, ensuring it survived long enough to continue breaking new ground over the decades. But those early titles aren’t always a lot of fun to play today. The original game sometimes felt cheap and rather bland, even near release. Its sequel had an interesting plot and ambitious new mechanics, but it confounded many players with unclear, non-linear objectives. Then Castlevania 3: Dracula’s Curse came around and perfected the formula, providing multiple heroes with lore (which Netflix later explored with an animated series) and unique play styles, along with diverging paths through gorgeous stages that pushed the NES hardware harder than ever before. It’s the finest single example of what Castlevania could be during that era, and well worth revisiting today.
2 Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse
Released: Oct. 15, 2026

Check our full Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse review for all the details, but the short version is this: you need to play the game. It respects the series’ history while mapping out a potential future we hope the developers will one day realize with follow-up titles. The 2.5D visuals give each area a new sense of depth, while enabling the satisfying Metroidvania mechanics players have enjoyed since Symphony of the Night changed the franchise forever. Fluid movement during combat, a killer soundtrack to match the moonlit ambience of the visuals, and a brave new hero all add up to one of the very finest entries the series has ever seen.
1 Castlevania: Symphony of the Night
Released: Oct. 2, 1997

Nearly 30 years after its release, there’s still no topping Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. It’s the game credited with taking Metroid’s design and fusing it with the gothic adventuring players associate with the Castlevania series. The sprawling castle was populated by nightmarish creatures, many of them familiar and many of them not. Stripped of his powerful weapons, Alucard explores the castle and seeks to put down his fearsome father once and for all. But as players learned, there’s much more to the adventure than the simple castle they glimpse beneath the moonlight. One of the happiest surprises in video games came when players looked at things through a new perspective, thanks to some holy spectacles. The shift in focus opened up an unfamiliar pathway, revealing that they weren’t even halfway done with their adventure. It was the game that kept on giving, and it still hasn’t stopped.

articles.headline: World of Warcraft Forever World First Level 60 Character Hits Cap Three Days After Launch
keyFacts: Team JokerD became the first to reach level 60 in World of Warcraft Forever just three days after the launch.
The team utilized Undead characters to leverage the modified Cannibalize ability and eliminate downtime during speedrunning.
Blizzard principal game designer Kris Zierhut stated that the game intends players to level multiple characters because early raids do not open until December 9.
body: World of Warcraft Forever is all about taking your time and exploring the world, rather than rushing to the endgame. But, despite the Forever team's insistence on taking your time and making friends, a WoW Forever player has already hit level 60.

Team JokerD, led by the eponymous streamer was the first team of characters to hit level 60, and the team was made up entirely of Undead characters and one Troll. The Undead race was important there, because Blizzard changed the Cannibalize ability to help you regenerate mana, which meant there was little to no downtime between massive pulls. I spent some time watching the streams of these speedrunners, and they'd gather entire groups of mobs to nuke them down with AoE abilities.

JokerD's claim to fame was being the world's first level 60 when World of Warcraft Classic launched back in 2019, so it's not super suprising that his team was the first to hit max level in Forever. There was plenty of competition this time around, but JokerD's team was pretty far ahead of the fray throughout the entire race. Even at the time of writing, the second place character who's not part of JokerD's team is Ksuper Worldfirst, who is still level 53.

However, while it's cool that these players have been able to hit max level already, there's not much of a reason to rush to endgame right now. The first raids, Barrow Deeps, Hyjal Summit and Onyxia's Lair, don't open until December 9, so players hitting level cap this weekend might find it hard to find what they should do next.

When I interviewed WoW Forever principal game designer Kris Zierhut , he made it pretty clear that Blizzard intends players to level multiple characters, and reinforced that leveling is a major part of the game. So, if you do manage to make it to level 60 super early and you run out of content before raids open, it might be worth it to start another character and take a different path to max level.

WoW Forever also had an extremely smooth launch , and was largely free of any major server problems. But, then again, Blizzard later came out and bragged that the game was running on more than 200TB of RAM, so it'd be a little concerning if the servers still buckled under the weight of players trying to log in.

articles.headline: GOP counts a few more wins in House races — but Democrats still have massive majority
keyFacts: House Republicans secured several midterm election wins on Friday, including races called for Jeff Hurd, Mark Lamb, and Anthony Constantino.

body: Republicans finally got some good news on Friday when a handful of midterm nailbiter elections were decided in their favor.
The Associated Press had called 254 races for Democrats and 162 for Republicans (up from 155 Thursday afternoon) as of Friday afternoon, with 19 House seats still up in the air.
The races called Friday included GOP wins for Rep. Jeff Hurd in Colorado, Mark Lamb in Arizona and Anthony Constantino in New York’s 21st Congressional District.
Constantino, who ran in retiring Rep. Elise Sefanik’s (R-NY) upstate district, had already declared himself the winner at his Election Night watch party.
Of the remaining House races too close to call, Democrats lead in about half of them — and they could further expand their sizable majority.
The incumbent Republicans in danger of being unseated include, Reps. Lauren Boebert (R-Colo.), Brand Finstad (R-Minn.), Scott DesJarlais (R-Tenn.) and Virginia Foxx (R-N.C.)
A Boebert campaign lawyer alleged “unusual voting patterns” in the congresswoman’s race against Democrat Eileen Laubacher late Thursday and said he is expecting it to head to a recount.

“Since election night, ballot returns have been trending in Congresswoman Boebert’s direction, consistently lowering the margin under one percentage point,” Scott Gessler, who is also Colorado’s former secretary of state, said in a statement. “We are investigating some very unusual voting patterns and expect this election to head to a recount, one way or another.”
Democrats have gained at least 42 seats.
On the Senate side, two races remain uncalled: Alaska and Mississippi.
Democrat Mary Peltola leads incumbent GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan in the Alaska race by 0.3 percentage points, or about 600 votes, with 74% of ballots counted in the ranked-choice contest.
In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom continues to lead incumbent GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde‑Smith by 0.3 percentage points, or about 2,500 votes, with 97% of ballots counted.

“We are not backing down,” Hyde‑Smith defiantly posted on X Friday. “This election is not over. Our team is working across Mississippi to monitor the remaining ballots and protect the integrity of the process.
“We will see this through to the very end!”
Democrats have thus far secured a 54-44 majority in the upper chamber.

articles.headline: Golden State Warriors’ Kristaps Porziņģis steps away from basketball over undisclosed health issue
keyFacts: Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis announced he is stepping away from basketball to prioritize his health.
Porziņģis did not disclose the specific nature of his health issue in his social media post.

body: Golden State Warriors center Kristaps Porziņģis announced he is stepping away from basketball to prioritize his health due to an undisclosed matter in a social media post on Friday.
Porziņģis did not reveal the nature of the issue in a message posted on his X account, and the 31-year-old did not make clear whether he will resume playing.
“I was really looking forward to running it with this group, but as I ramped up, my body didn’t respond the way I anticipated,” Porziņģis wrote.

“I’m doing good, but I know what it takes, and I’m not where I want to be to perform at the level I expect from myself,” he added. “At this point, I’ve made the decision to prioritize my health and step away from the game I love.”
Selected fourth overall by the New York Knicks in the 2015 draft, Porziņģis was on his sixth team in 11 seasons.

The issue appears to date to last season, when the Latvian missed significant time after being acquired by Golden State in a trade with Atlanta. The Warriors, however, fully anticipated Porziņģis would be ready for this season after signing him to a two-year, $40m contract in late June.
Porziņģis’ status has been uncertain since late September, when the Warriors announced he would be out indefinitely with a health issue and would not travel with the team to Hawaii for training camp.

On 14 October, the team said Porziņģis would spend time with staff and teammates in some capacity while still out indefinitely after he met with general manager Mike Dunleavy and vice-president of player health and performance Dr Rick Celebrini a day earlier.

A week later, the Warriors reversed course, saying Porziņģis would not be with the team for “the immediate future”, with coach Steve Kerr providing no further insight ahead of the team’s season opener at the Los Angeles Lakers.
In his message, Porziņģis said he intends to work with the Warriors to “find a solution that makes sense”.
He closed his message by writing: “I’m thankful to my family and close ones for always being there. Much appreciation to all of you for the support. Onwards and upwards.”

articles.headline: Alpine Linux and OpenSSH patch flaw that’s as bad as it can get
keyFacts: Alpine Linux and other musl-based distributions have an OpenSSH authentication bypass vulnerability caused by a C library error handling flaw.
Attackers can log into key-only accounts by sending a specific length password if certain default configurations are enabled.
Alpine released patched software versions, and administrators must upgrade packages and restart the SSH daemon immediately.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- An ancient bug is affecting Alpine Linux and a few other Linux distros.
- It’s about as bad as it can get.
- You must patch ASAP, and then restart the patched software.

The perfect nightmare scenario for a Linux server is when all an attacker needs to do is reach the server’s Secure Shell (SSH) port, waltz right in, and take it over. That’s what happened to Alpine Linux, the popular, lightweight Linux server. Adding insult to injury, this happened only days after Alpine Linux dodged a security hole-sized bullet to its GitLab implementation.
How the attack works
As security engineer Gregory Bryant explained in his LinkedIn post:
Most authentication bypasses come from complex logic chains, but yesterday’s Alpine Linux OpenSSH vulnerability (CVE-2026-123158) comes down to a single character: *.”

If you run Alpine Linux (or another musl-based distro) with the default openssh-server package (no Pluggable Authentication Modules (PAM)) and PasswordAuthentication enabled, an attacker can log into password-disabled, or key-only accounts simply by sending a password between 257 and 1024 bytes long.
That’s it. That’s all.

Alpine Linux isn’t the only operating system that uses musl, a lightweight version of the standard C library (libc). Other operating systems that use musl and are potentially vulnerable include Adélie Linux; Void Linux; Sabotage Linux; OpenWrt, an Android variant, and the Yocto Project, which is used to build embedded Linux distributions.

Wind River, which produces the commercial embedded Linux distro, Wind River Linux, is also looking into the issue. A company representative told me, “Wind River takes security seriously. We are actively reviewing the reported vulnerability and assessing its potential impact. We will take appropriate action as needed.”

Behind the scenes, when OpenSSH is built without PAM, it verifies passwords by hashing the password attempt using the C library’s crypt() function. It then compares the result to the account’s stored password field. So far, so good.

But when a key is longer than 256 bytes, musl’s crypt() function returns the string * as an error indicator. That is also what the password field holds for any account with no password, such as a key-only account. Thus, the “hash” matches and the login succeeds, and the attacker walks in.

To exploit it, an attacker only needs the name of such an account. The attacker also needs at least one other account on the machine with a 5 or 6 password hash, and then to send a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes. According to Alpine, one user with a password is enough to make every passwordless account accessible.
In Linux systems that use glibc’s crypt(), which is almost all of them, the same attempt would return NULL on error, which sshd already rejects, so Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, etc., aren’t affected.
According to *sshole, the group that uncovered the problem, this is a side effect that has been hiding since 2016.
Who’s exposed
Alpine said every release it checked is affected: 3.21 through 3.24, edge, and the older 3.16 to 3.20 branches. Exposure requires the following:
- The openssh-server package, which is built without PAM, or openssh-server-pam with UsePAM no.
- PasswordAuthentication set to yes, which is the OpenSSH default.
- An account with * as its password field, and another account with a 5 or 6 hash.

Root is not directly exposed in most cases. It has shipped as root:* in the base image since about Alpine 3.16, but OpenSSH’s default PermitRootLogin prohibit-password blocks it. Another account that can become root, for example through doas, still gives an attacker a route to root.

Alpine singled out its official tiny-cloud images, versions 3.18.11 through 3.24.3, as especially vulnerable. These ship with an alpine user with a * password field and passwordless doas. They are safe on first boot but become exploitable once any 6 hash exists on the machine. That can happen when an administrator sets a console password or when user data adds a user with a hashed password, which means, essentially, all of them.
Alpine said these are not affected:
- Containers that do not run sshd.
- Systems with password authentication disabled.
- Systems using openssh-server-pam with UsePAM yes.
- Locked accounts with! in the password field.
- Cloud images configured through cloud-init, which writes PasswordAuthentication no.
The fix

Alpine released 3.21.10, 3.22.8, 3.23.8 and 3.24.4 on Thursday, with the OpenSSH fix among the security changes. It also published fixed packages for each release back to 3.16. Alpine 3.21 reached end of support on Nov. 1.

The just-released OpenSSH 10.6p2 avoids the problem in sshd. Alpine’s stable branches carry a patch for the same problem. You should run apk upgrade -U -a and then restart the daemon with rc-service sshd restart. Alpine stressed that upgrading the package does not replace the running daemon. Anyone who cannot update should set PasswordAuthentication no and restart sshd, after confirming that key login works.

To check for an attack, Alpine told administrators to search /var/log/messages for “Accepted password for” lines that name an account with no password. It also advised reviewing dedicated OpenBSD application subexecutor (doas) use and recently created users, files, and authorized keys. “If you cannot rule out a login, treat the machine as compromised.” Just what you wanted for your weekend, I know, but here we are.

articles.headline: Six tries and a big win - but were Ireland ruthless?
keyFacts: Ireland defeated Argentina 42-12 with six tries in Dublin, though head coach Andy Farrell stated his team missed a chance to be ruthless.
Captain Dan Sheehan, Robert Baloucoune, Sean Jansen, Josh van der Flier, and Mack Hansen all sustained injuries during the match.
Ireland will play Fiji in Dublin on 14 November before facing South Africa later in the international window.
body: - Published
Before Ireland's Nations Championship game with Argentina, head coach Andy Farrell had been honest about where his side are less than a year out from the World Cup.

He admitted his team must improve if they are to challenge in Australia next year - a stark contrast to four years ago when they were riding the crest of a wave before they fell short in the quarter-finals.
Despite Mateo Carreras' early try, Ireland had far too much for Los Pumas in Dublin as they ran out 42-12 winners under the Friday night lights.
Hugo Keenan stole the headlines with his hat-trick, while Dan Sheehan, Sam Prendergast and Ronan Kelleher also crossed.
But despite scoring six tries and winning by a 30-point margin, Farrell was left wanting more.
Ireland had 59% territory throughout the game, and also edged possession, but did not score after the 55th minute when Kelleher rounded off a rolling maul.
"The scoreline is a good one because not many teams do that to Argentina, they are a dangerous side," Farrell said.
"I thought there was outstanding stuff and some clinical stuff, but I think the story of the game is we missed a chance to be ruthless.
"Having said that, the opportunities we had in the right end of the field showed the dominance in field position and territory."
One concern for Farrell will be an injury list - and a lengthy one at that.
Captain Dan Sheehan was forced off in the first half after he failed a head injury assessment, although Farrell said he "seems fine in the dressing room".
Wing Robert Baloucoune was forced off with a knock, while Sean Jansen sustained a "bang" to his knee and Josh van der Flier and Mack Hansen both have ankle concerns.
The injuries to Baloucoune, who went off in the 58th minute, and Hansen, who continued after receiving treatment, will be particularly concerning after the performance of Farrell's back three.

They had only played once together before, four years ago against South Africa, and Keenan's first try of the evening came off the back of a flowing move, when Baloucoune powered into space and found Hansen, who in turn set up the full-back to score.
That was the catalyst for Ireland's turnaround - and a hat-trick for Keenan in his first home match since the 2025 Six Nations came a year since Hansen's treble against Australia in Dublin.
All of Farrell's back three trio have struggled with injuries in the past year, and Friday's win was a glimpse of Ireland's attacking potential if they can stay fit and in form.
"I thought back three outstanding. Hugo Keenan, 22 months since he played here and didn't remember what side of the pitch we warmed up, which was a bit of an insult.
"He was immense. Same with Mack and Rob. They pace they put onto the ball and they were a threat. I'm delighted with the back three."
Ireland 'weathered the storm'
Beirne said that Argentina "came out firing" in Dublin as they chased a first away win over Ireland, something that came as no surprise to the Irish pack.
"We weathered the storm and got into how we wanted to play the game," said Beirne.
"What was pleasing about that was some of those tries were proper team tries and everyone was involved with them. That was the biggest takeaway from the game that."
But, like Farrell, the second row believes there is more to come at the attacking end of the pitch.
"We probably came away a little bit frustrated because we felt we didn't capitalise on a lot of the territory at the end of the game and the chances we had.
"That shows how good a performance it was to come away feeling like that."
After a bruising opener, Farrell will be forced to assess his squad ahead of Fiji's visit to Dublin on 14 November.
After that, world champions South Africa will be a stern test before the finals weekend in London to round out the international window.
He had offered Craig Casey a chance to impress at scrum-half as first-choice Jamison Gibson-Park returns to full fitness, and he impressed after a slow start.
Ulster back row Nick Timoney also put in a big performance, while Prendergast's showing at fly-half was also largely positive as he put his stamp on the 10 jersey.
When asked if the performances gave him food for thought for selections for the rest of the window, Farrell said: "Definitely, 100%.
"That's exactly what you are after going into next week.
"Having some good competition, we've had it for 10 days in training so how they performed highlights how they have been training.
"Whatever side we pick next week, they'll be competing to play the following week."

articles.headline: OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
keyFacts: OpenAI reached a valuation of $1.25 trillion after raising $11 billion in a new funding round reported by Bloomberg.
CEO Sam Altman stated that OpenAI is prioritizing model safety and holding off on an initial public offering for now.
Rival company Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public last week.
body: OpenAI is now valued at $1.25 trillion in a new round of funding that has raised another $11 billion, according to Bloomberg. That would make it one of the world’s most valuable companies, not long after raising $122 billion from investors in March at a valuation of $852 billion.
OpenAI valued at $1.25 trillion, as rival Anthropic nears its IPO
CEO Sam Altman said recently that OpenAI is prioritizing safety instead of going ‘guns blazing’ toward an IPO.

Echoing FT and Wall Street Journal reports from last week, Bloomberg says OpenAI is still pursuing additional investments that could increase the amount to $20 billion, and that it had initially hoped to raise as much as $30 billion at a higher valuation of $1.4 trillion. That was before tech stocks dropped, and the results of the midterms showed how much public opinion has turned against AI companies and data center projects.

OpenAI’s rival Anthropic filed its S-1 to go public last week. Earlier this year, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said it’s holding off on its own IPO until it can make more confident claims about its models’ safety. He didn’t give a specific timeline for the IPO, but said at the time, “I think it’s also kind of bad for the world if OpenAI waits too long to go public.”

articles.headline: Democrats blast Trump’s decision to appoint Stephen Miller as chief of staff in wake of Republican midterm rout – live
keyFacts: Donald Trump appointed adviser Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff after Republican midterm election losses.
Democrats and some Republicans condemned the promotion, citing Miller's role as the architect of Trump's hardline deportation agenda.
Miller will start his new role on November 9, while Democrats stated they will investigate him in Congress.
body: Democrats blast Trump’s decision to appoint Stephen Miller as chief of staff in wake of Republican midterm rout – live
Chuck Schumer says the move to promote the controversial immigration hardliner shows that Donald Trump ‘learned nothing from his historic defeat’ in the midterms

Stephen Miller, one of Donald Trump’s fiercest allies and architect of the administration’s hardline deportation agenda, will now be the White House chief of staff. The role is a promotion for Miller, who currently serves as an adviser. Trump said that Miller will start the job on Monday 9 November, less than a week after Republicans’ crushing defeat in the midterm elections.

Wiles will now take a role in Trump’s political operation, which includes his Super Pac Maga Inc. On social media, she said that serving the president has been “the honor of a lifetime”. Wiles has been in the president’s orbit for over a decade, and prior to her role at the White House, she managed, alongside Chris LaCivita, Trump’s winning 2024 presidential campaign.

Trump later told reporters that he decided to promote Miller because he“wanted to make a change”. He praised Wiles, and said that Miller had been by his side “from the beginning”. “Sometimes in life you have to make moves,” the president said.

Meanwhile, Democrats blasted Trump’s decision, after Republicans faced a drubbing in the midterm elections. Chuck Schumer, the Senate minority leader, said that the president “learned nothing from his historic defeat”, and Congressman Robert Garcia – poised to be the chair of the House oversight committee – advised Miller to “lawyer up”. Garcia said that in the majority, Democrats on his panel will “continue to investigate [Stephen] Miller for his misconduct, and we will fight against his hateful policies in Congress and the courts”.

Reading aloud from prepared remarks to NASA officials at Cape Canaveral in Florida on Friday, Donald Trump ran through a list of what he called evidence that Americans were “the greatest pioneers explorers, inventors and innovators who ever lived.”

“America is the nation that dreamed and created the modern world,” Trump said, peering at a teleprompter from beneath a USA cap. “We laid the railroads, harnessed electricity and invented the lightbulb, the telephone, the airplane, the assembly line, the television, the microchip, the personal computer, the internet, GPS, the smartphone, and almost every other thing- think of it – almost every other thing that’s worth mentioning.”

He then looked out at the audience and veered off-script to comment: “That’s a cool list, though, when you think, huh? How about a little piece of each of them? Wouldn’t that be nice? You wouldn’t be sitting here right now. You’d be someplace else.”

The president then returned to his prepared remarks, looking back at the teleprompter and saying: “We charted the human genome to cure diseases,” but stumbled badly over the word “genome” which he pronounced “guh-nome”.

Despite Trump’s attempt to claim that the US deserves credit for sequencing all the DNA in human chromosomes, the Human Genome Project was, in fact, the work of an international network of geneticists.
Trump expresses satisfaction at stock market plunge after Republican losses in midterms, deflects blame from himself

Donald Trump, remarkably, gave yet another speech on Friday, delivering remarks at the John F. Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida in his official capacity as president, which were, nonetheless, threaded through with partisan political talking points.

The president emerged to the theme tune from his rallies, God Bless the USA, and mimed dancing, before starting his speech by celebrating the victories of two Florida Republicans, Byron Donalds, the governor-elect, and senator Ashley Moody.
The pair were the only two candidates Trump rallied for in the past month who won competitive races.

He then praised members of his administration who were present, singling out the US ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, for “the way you took on, the Cubans”. Waltz was recently engaged in a spat with a Cuban official at the UN which played on heavy rotation on Fox News, the president’s window on the world.

Trump then suggested that he was glad that the US stock market plunged after the Republican wipeout at the ballot box, on fears that companies building AI data centers might not be as free to push ahead with regulation by a Democratic Congress.

“Yesterday, you know, our country lost $3 trillion, all because of an election,” Trump said. “If we were to gain $3 trillion, I probably would have been more unhappy. But you know what that means; that means that they thought somebody else did well in an election.”
“By the way, I was not on the ballot, just in case you had any question,” he added. “Because if we were on the ballot, we would’ve won but we weren’t.”
Senator Chris Murphy discharged from hospital after stroke as doctor says he expects full recovery

Senator Chris Murphy was released from a hospital on Friday following treatment for a stroke and plans to spend several weeks at a rehabilitation center as he works to recover, the Connecticut Democrat said in a statement.

“Thank you for the outpouring of support my family and I have received over the last few days,” Murphy said. “I want to be direct with you, so here is my diagnosis. Last Saturday afternoon, I felt something was not right with my body and called 9-1-1 out of an abundance of caution, and I’m glad I did. I was diagnosed with a small bleed in the thalamus region of my brain.”

“The doctors are very encouraged by the progress I’ve made so far. In order to take my recovery seriously and get back to work on the quickest timeline possible, I will be spending several weeks at a rehabilitation center after being discharged from the hospital today,” he continued.

The senator also released a statement from Dr Jose Suarez, the chief of neurosciences critical care at the Johns Hopkins Hospital. “Senator Murphy experienced a small hemorrhagic stroke. He has shown tremendous progress, and at the current rate of improvement, we expect that he will make a full recovery following rehabilitation,” the doctor said.
Indiana Republican congressman reportedly calls Trump's promotion of Stephen Miller to chief of staff 'a horrible decision'

The morning after the midterm wave that swept away dozens of his colleagues, congressman Marlin Stutzman, an Indiana Republican who held his seat, told voters that Donald Trump’s mass deportation agenda was a major factor, and called on the president to fire its architect, Stephen Miller.

“The press ran with it, the Democrats ran with it, and it looked bad on us – the deportation effort,” Stutzman said on Wednesday. “President Obama deported more illegals than what President Trump has. But you know what? he didn’t he didn’t go out and talk about it the way that, you know, we did. I mean, frankly, I think Stephen Miller should be fired this morning. I mean, there needs to be some changs at hte White House.”
Asked by Semafor on Friday what he made of Trump’s decision to not fire but promote Miller, Stutzman told the outlet it was a “horrible decision.”

Several newly elected Democrats and Senator Bernie Sanders have renewed calls for datacenter moratoriums in the days after the US midterm elections. The sweeping Democratic victory, which was buoyed in part by backlash to the tech industry, has added momentum to efforts to slow down the multi-trillion-dollar buildout of the controversial facilities.

On the social media platform X, Sanders posted a call for an immediate national datacenter moratorium this week. “Americans don’t want Big Tech oligarchs wrecking the environment, gutting jobs and threatening humanity’s future,” Sanders said on Wednesday.
Sanders was joined by several Democrats, including Representative Yassamin Ansari of Arizona – a state where Elon Musk’s SpaceX has proposed a datacenter project that would span more than 700 acres.

“Top of the Democratic agenda on day 1 needs to be a pause on advanced AI development, regulation of this out of control industry, and a ban on artificial superintelligence,” Ansari posted Wednesday on X. Musk mocked her post in a retweet, and the two sparred, with Ansari forecasting congressional hearings, telling the centi-billionaire: “See you soon.”

The pushback to the buildout of datacenters, which tech companies need to power the AI products that have become central to their businesses, was one of the most visible issues of the midterms. Opposition to datacenters figured heavily in campaigns across the US, while voters passed dozens of local ballot measures aimed at restricting datacenter projects in their states.
Add congressman Don Beyer, a Virginia Democrat, to the ranks of those deeply alarmed at Donald Trump naming Stephen Miller his new White House chief of staff.
“Trump’s elevation of Stephen Miller doubles down on the politics of hatred, lawlessness, and failure that the American people soundly rejected three days ago,” Beyer said in a statement.
He continued:

“Stephen Miller is the architect of Trump’s immigration policies that plunged quiet American communities into violence. At Miller’s direction, peaceful, law-abiding people have been seized from their families and imprisoned or deported for minor civil offenses, and American citizens who protested these actions have been beaten up and even killed by masked paramilitary thugs. Miller is also the ‘brains’ behind the illegal, extrajudicial murders of people in the Caribbean and the Pacific, many of whom may have done nothing wrong. He frequently promised in 2024 that Trump would focus on the economy and avoid new wars, and then became an ardent defender of Trump’s foolish, unpopular attacks on Iran and other countries.

“Stephen Miller embodies the worst elements of the Trump presidency. His promotion shows that Trump has learned nothing from his electoral debacle and has no intention of even trying to work constructively with the next Congress. But Trump and his Republican allies who continue to embrace the politics of hate, division, and chaos are wildly out of step with what the American people want, and they will keep suffering more defeats until they listen.”

Miles Taylor, who served as chief of staff at the Department of Homeland Security during Donald Trump’s first term, and wrote in an anonymous, 2018 New York Times Op-Ed article that he was “working diligently from within” the Trump administration “to frustrate parts of his agenda and his worst inclinations,” has weighed in on the danger of a White House run by Stephen Miller.
Taylor, who later resigned to join the ranks of anti-Trump Republican memoirists and podcasters, warned on Friday:

I spent two years working with Stephen Miller. His appointment as White House chief of staff is among the most dangerous personnel decisions in the history of our republic. I say that without reservation.
Republican congressman Mark Harris has narrowly won reelection to House in North Carolina’s eighth congressional district, defeating Democrat Colby Watson by just over 5,000 votes.

Democrats have won nine House seats in North Carolina so far, to just one for Republicans, with four races still too close to call, including one in which a Democrat leads a Republican incumbent by just 99 votes.
As voters reject Trump's agenda, Stephen Miller says president 'has single-handedly saved America from those who would destroy it'

The elevation of Stephen Miller, the architect of Donald Trump’s brutal and unpopular mass deportation agenda, to White House chief of staff suggests that the president has no intention of rolling back the crackdown, even after voters delivered a sweeping rebuke by electing Democrats to every House seat along the US border with Mexico.
Miller’s appointment has been widely condemned by Democrats, and some Republicans, but the man himself said in a statement that he is “honored beyond words” to run the White House.

“President Trump is the most transformative political leader in American History — and he has single-handedly saved America from those who would destroy it,” Miller said, referring to the incoming Democratic majority in both houses of Congress in typically extreme fashion.

“The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President and defend this magnificent Republic,” Miller added, in a clear signal that the final two years of Trump’s presidency will pit a maximally combative White House against Congress.
The NAACP’s president, Derrick Johnson, has this to say about the elevation of Stephen Miller, a longtime promoter of white nationalism, to the role of White House chief of staff:
“Stephen Miller belongs nowhere near the Oval Office. He belongs before a judge. He’s a thug who will be remembered as the architect of Trump’s vile and authoritarian regime.”
Hegseth and RFK Jr welcome Miller's promotion to White House chief of staff

Pete Hegseth, the embattled former Fox weekend anchor turned US defense secretary who could face an impeachment vote as soon as next week, was quick to praise new White House chief of staff Stephen Miller on social media, posting a meme of the two men together, with the caption “Stand. Fight. Defend the Republic.” Hegseth tagged both Miller and the White House on X, Elon Musk’s rebranded, rightwing Twitter, to make sure they were aware of his post.

Hegseth, who appears to be leading a coordinated social-media campaign to save his job, used the same caption for a previous post on Thursday, which featured images of himself and one of Donald Trump raising his fist moments after surviving an assassination attempt in 2024.

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the health secretary, quickly followed with a post welcoming Miller’s appointment as a supporter of the so-called Make America Health Again movement. “Next to me, Stephen Miller is the strongest MAHA supporter in the administration,” Kennedy wrote. “It’s time to unleash the Kraken.”

articles.headline: Here's what's in Path of Exile 2’s huge 1.0 release, coming in December
keyFacts: Path of Exile 2 will release its full 1.0 version on December 11 after two years of early access.
The update adds two new classes, the Shadow and the Duelist, alongside acts five and six to complete the campaign.
The release introduces a new league mechanic called Conquerors of Wraeclast, featuring base building, army recruitment, and castle battles.
body: Path of Exile 2's full release is out on December 11, and coming with it are two new classes, two new acts, a new league, tons of new monsters, bosses, battles, endgame changes, gem updates, atlas and skill tree updates, a new pinnacle boss, base types, uniques, and, I don't know, probably a kitchen sink or something. Let's go over it.

First of all, we'll have two new classes: the Shadow and the Duelist. With them, we'll get all new skill gems for daggers and swords, with tons of new builds available. Daggers introduce new mechanics around stealth, traps, shadow skills with clones that attack with you, and classic skills like blade vortex and fire trap.

The Duelist will introduce swords, and with it fan favorite skills like cyclone and hemorrhage. With swords we'll be able to use stances like blood and sand or ready stance. Add to this being able to two-hand, dual wield, or sword and board and swords look to add a huge amount of mechanical complexity.

After two years of early access, the campaign will finally be fully finished. Acts five and six will complete our story of chasing the Beast through the world, with a return to Oriath and beyond. The campaign will also feature new bespoke rare monsters with their own abilities, appearances, and even mods. In addition, the campaign will feature an introduction to the league mechanic for 1.0, Conquerors of Wraeclast.

The league will feature a base building mechanic, where you recruit armies and build up a castle. As you progress through the campaign, you'll recruit armies to battle against enemy armies. There are over 70 points of interest throughout the campaign that let you recruit new types of soldiers for your army, and battle through to kill the boss and get loot.

As you progress your base, you can recruit commanders that will be able to take your recruits and fight battles for you. Like Kingsmarch in Path of Exile 1, these commanders can run maps for you, letting you convert your gold into progress through the atlas and lots of loot. Your castle gets upgraded just like Heroes of Might and Magic, with a beautiful base that you can spend gold to upgrade.

After all the pinnacle bosses and campaign, you can use your armies to battle against other players. Depending on which of the three factions you choose to join (Karui, Ezomyte, or Marraketh), you can battle to take control of various castles around the atlas. As long as your faction controls a castle, you can travel to it on the Atlas to skip around and get to sweet new maps, and you'll receive additional item rarity. It also unlocks hunting grounds nearby that feature rare monsters with increased loot. You'll be able to use currency you find in battle to craft gear, a system which lets you pick mods to remove and reroll into new fractured mods.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
All of the new campaign areas feature new bosses, which you'll also face in the endgame in over 25 new maps.

The endgame has been updated as well—in addition to being able to use castles to jump around the atlas, the atlas skill tree has been substantially changed. Instead of 300+ nodes, it's been trimmed way down to about 70. If you beeline the skills, you should end up with about 50 of 70 by the time you battle against the Arbiter of Divinity.

Tons of gems have been updated. Not only are we getting new gems for daggers and swords, but they've added new skills for existing weapons as well. Support gems have been overhauled so that they're more useful as well, like all of the different elemental penetration gems being rolled into one called elemental penetration. Support gems like brutality are also better, with less of a penalty for chaos damage. Chain support becomes just an upgrade, without the penalty to damage on the initial hit.

The passive tree has had huge changes. In addition to a bunch of new nodes, they've changed how jewels work. Instead of always being located on the travel nodes on the outside of the tree, they'll be located in actual skill clusters. Hopefully this will prevent all of our endgame skill trees looking the same, with a big circle maximizing jewel slots and nothing else.

With tons of new items including base types and uniques, there will be lots of new loot to find. Some of the base types look insanely powerful, like an armor that makes you immune to curses. They've overhauled over 70 uniques and added about 40 more, which should make finding uniques way more exciting, especially in the campaign.

Taken all together, 1.0 looks like it will be an incredible moment for Path of Exile 2, both for players who've been waiting to play it, and for those of us who already have hundreds or thousands of hours in the ARPG. The full release of Path of Exile 2 will be available on December 11.
